# Seed-content generation prompt (for ChatGPT or any external model)

**Why this exists.** The demo's seed content is placeholder text (`"An editorial
piece about hiking — issue 3."`). That is fine for exercising plumbing but useless
for evaluating an AI feature: a subject-line or content-suggestion task fed
placeholder text can only produce generic output, so the test returns a **false
negative** — it looks like the feature failed when in fact the input carried no
signal.

**Why an external model.** Content generated by the same model we are testing makes
the test easier than reality — AI prose is already on-the-nose and unusually easy for
AI to summarise. Generating it elsewhere is not a perfect control, but it is a
meaningfully harder test. For the honest version, drop in one or two genuinely
human-written pieces later.

## How to use

1. Paste the prompt below into ChatGPT (or any model).
2. Save the result as a `.csv` file.
3. Import it: `./venv/bin/python scripts/import_content_csv.py <file>.csv`

`seed_content_template.csv` in this directory is a working two-row example — it
shows the exact format **and** the quality bar.

---

## The prompt

````
You are an editor for a travel newsletter. Produce seed content records as CSV.

FORMAT — exactly these columns, in this order, with a header row:

title,description,headline_medium,body_medium,button_label,button_url,image_url,image_alt,categories

Rules for each column:
- title            — the record's internal name. Max 255 chars. Usually identical to headline_medium.
- description      — one sentence, max 500 chars, describing what the piece covers.
- headline_medium  — the headline as it appears in the email.
- body_medium      — the body copy. 60–100 words. This is the important one; see QUALITY below.
- button_label     — 2–4 words, action-oriented ("See the routes", "Read the Tuesday plan").
- button_url       — use https://example.com/<slug>
- image_url        — use https://example.com/img/<slug>.jpg
- image_alt        — short literal description of the image.
- categories       — pipe-separated Name:Score pairs, e.g. Hiking:10|Nature:7|Food:4
                     Score is 0–10 and expresses how strongly the piece belongs to that
                     category. Give each record 1 primary category (score 8–10) and 1–3
                     secondary ones (score 3–7).

CATEGORIES — use ONLY these names, spelled exactly like this:
Beach, City, Nature, Hiking, Family, Culture, Food, Wellness, Adventure,
Luxury, Budget, Winter, Nightlife, Wildlife

QUALITY — this is the whole point of the exercise:
- Write like a real editor, not like marketing copy. Concrete beats enthusiastic.
- Every piece must contain at least two SPECIFIC, checkable-sounding details:
  a place name, an opening time, a price, a distance, a season, a local quirk.
- No filler openers ("Discover the magic of…", "Whether you're a seasoned…").
- No exclamation marks. No second-person hard sell.
- Vary sentence length. It is fine to be dry or slightly opinionated.
- Each record must be about a DIFFERENT place or angle. No near-duplicates.

QUANTITY — produce [N] records, spread across the categories so that every
category above is the primary category of at least one record.

OUTPUT — raw CSV only, no commentary before or after. Quote every field with
double quotes. Escape internal double quotes by doubling them.
````

Replace `[N]` with how many you want (30–50 gives the decision engine real choices
across 14 categories).

---

## Notes

- The importer matches categories **by name** against the categories already in the
  database, so existing categories are preserved — nothing is renamed or recreated.
- The importer **adds** records; it does not delete. Existing placeholder records
  stay until you remove or deactivate them (see the "no deactivate option" bug in
  `docs/backlog.md`).
- Re-running the importer with the same file is safe: records whose `title` already
  exists are skipped.
- Content records are **not personal data**, so realistic content here does not
  conflict with [[ADR-143 — AI-Assisted Development Boundary]] — it is *recipient*
  data that must be pseudonymized, not editorial content.
